paper_title: DeltaEdit Enhancing Sequential Editing in Large Language Models by   Controlling Superimposed Noise
caption: The changes in Efficacytop (the rate of successfully maximizing the object's probability) and noise_E with the number of edits. The top figure displays results for GPT2-XL using AlphaEdit and MEMIT, while the bottom figure shows results for LLaMA3-8B using only AlphaEdit. MEMIT is excluded for LLaMA3-8B due to its excessively high noise_E, making visualization difficult.
model_annotation: The line chart illustrates the relationship between the number of edits (x-axis) and two performance metrics—Efficacy_top (left y-axis) and noise_E (right y-axis)—for the LLaMA3-8B model using the AlphaEdit method. The x-axis, labeled “Number of edits,” spans from 0 to 3000 with tick marks at intervals of 500. The left y-axis, labeled “Efficacy_top,” ranges from 75 to 100 in increments of 5 and represents the rate of successfully maximizing the target token’s probability. The right y-axis, labeled “noise_E,” spans from 0 to 6 in increments of 1 and quantifies the superimposed noise introduced during editing. Two lines are plotted: “AlphaEdit Efficacy_top,” shown as a dashed red line with square markers, begins at approximately 97.5 when edits = 0 and declines steadily to about 77.5 at 3000 edits. “AlphaEdit noise_E,” shown as a solid red line with circular markers, starts near 0.5 at 0 edits and increases monotonically to approximately 5.5 at 3000 edits. The chart demonstrates an inverse relationship between efficacy and noise as the number of edits increases, with no other methods or models included for comparison in this subplot.
